headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network defaults create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks between n8n and Roo Code.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can write workflow outputs to the server filesystem and orchestrate tools; Roo Code reads workspace files and can use MCP or browser outputs. A malicious or malformed n8n-produced file can be treated as trusted input by Roo Code, creating an injection path. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF n8n writes attacker-controlled text into a file that Roo Code later opens as instructions, injection is possible.
IF the two agents exchange content through a shared workspace or synced folder, prompt injection risk increases.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Require manual review of any file passed from n8n to Roo Code.
Strip instruction-like text from n8n outputs before handoff.
Use a provenance tag or filename convention for machine-generated artifacts.
requires-engineering: add content filtering or signed handoff metadata.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad filesystem read/write and broad network egress. n8n touches whatever the workflow processes, while Roo Code touches source code and browser screenshots; if they share a workspace or connected systems, sensitive data can flow from one into the other and then out via APIs. This is a default-capable leakage pathway, not merely unusual configuration.
conditions: IF n8n processes secrets, customer data, or regulated records in a shared workspace, Roo Code can read them.
IF Roo Code sends workspace contents or screenshots to a configured model API, data can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces and credentials.
Disable or restrict file sharing between the two agents.
Redact secrets before Roo Code opens files.
Limit Roo Code to a narrow project folder.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP or egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; n8n runs server-side with execute-command capability, while Roo Code runs as the user with terminal exec and workspace writes. If they target the same directory, concurrent edits and command execution can overwrite each other or corrupt state. The overlap is broad and dangerous by default when co-located.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory, file clobbering or race conditions can occur.
IF Roo Code modifies git state while n8n writes generated files into the repo, conflicts can corrupt commits or workflows.
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories.
Pause one agent before the other writes shared files.
Use git branches or separate clones.
Add lock files around shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n is an orchestration layer that can emit workflow outputs, and Roo Code can act on files and terminal commands. If Roo Code treats n8n output as authoritative, a mistaken or adversarial n8n result can cascade into code changes, browser actions, or shell execution. The pair therefore has a strong default pathway from generated output to downstream action.
conditions: IF Roo Code consumes n8n-generated text without verification, errors can propagate into actions.
IF n8n produces prompts, configs, or commands that Roo Code executes, downstream harm can be immediate.
mitigations: Require human approval before Roo Code acts on n8n output.
Validate n8n outputs against a schema.
Use a checksum or signature on handoff files.
Keep n8n outputs advisory, not executable.
requires-engineering: add policy checks before tool execution.

E_compliance.rationale: n8n handles whatever the workflow processes on its server, while Roo Code handles source code, screenshots, and model-provider API keys in a VS Code workspace. If regulated data or secrets are present, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches across server-side workflow storage and local IDE storage. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed in n8n and then copied into Roo Code's workspace, retention and access controls may diverge.
IF model-provider keys or workflow secrets are stored in shared files, compliance obligations may be breached.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared files.
Store secrets only in dedicated secret managers.
Review retention settings for both tools.
Use separate environments for production and development data.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
